data.title: Women's quota Bill seeks 50% rise in LS, Assembly seats; freeze till 2051
data.description:
The Centre has proposed a 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats for every state and Union territory, and in the strength of their Legislative Assemblies, to implement one-third reservation for women, with the revised seat allocations and constituency boundaries to remain in place until 2051.

The Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, slated for introduction in the Lok Sabha on Monday, seeks to raise the House's maximum strength to 850, with up to 815 members from states and 35 from Union territories. It also proposes to raise the ceiling on the size of a state Assembly from 500 to 650.

 

"The objective of the present Bill is to give immediate effect to one-third reservation for women, including women belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, in the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies of the states and the Union territories, through a delimitation exercise," the Bill's Statement of Objects and Reasons says.

It says the exercise "shall provide for an increase of 50 per cent in the number of seats in the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies of the states and Union territories, over and above the number of seats existing immediately before such delimitation".

The Bill adds that the quota would run for 15 years from the commencement of the 2023 amendment, with Parliament empowered to extend it by law.

Parliament would also determine the authority and manner for rotating the seats reserved for women.

The 2023 women's reservation law ties the quota's rollout to delimitation after publication of figures from the first census taken after that law comes into force.

The new Bill would trigger the quota after the first delimitation under the proposed amendment, using the latest published census figures available at its commencement to redraw constituency boundaries.

The Statement of Objects and Reasons says "the allocation of seats and the division into territorial constituencies so readjusted" would "continue until the year 2051".

data.title: Awareness gaps, compliance hurdles weigh on FTA utilisation: Experts
data.description:
The low utilisation of benefits under India’s free trade agreements (FTAs) reflects a combination of limited exporter awareness, procedural hurdles and difficulties in meeting stringent overseas standards, trade experts said on Friday, after Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra flagged that only 20-30 per cent of eligible Indian exports use preferential tariffs under such pacts.
 
The problem is particularly acute among micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), which often lack the financial resources and expertise to meet compliance, certification and packaging requirements in developed markets such as the European Union, Japan and Australia. Experts said improving utilisation would require targeted government outreach, access to trade consultants, affordable compliance support and assistance in navigating foreign regulations.
 
India, so far, has signed 17 FTAs with its trading partners, including seven modern trade agreements since 2021: With Mauritius, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Australia, the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), the UK, Oman and New Zealand.
 
The government has not made FTA utilisation data public. However, Indian exporters, according to industry sources, have made only modest gains from older agreements signed 15-16 years ago with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean), Japan and South Korea.
 
Among the key challenges are the cumbersome process of obtaining certificates of origin and related verification requirements, limited awareness of preferential tariff benefits and non-tariff barriers, including compliance with product standards.
 
India’s relatively high tariff levels compared with those of developed economies have also created an imbalance in the use of trade agreements. Since India started with higher tariffs, its duty reductions on some products have been steeper than those offered by developed-country partners, giving the latter greater incentives to use preferential access to the Indian market, industry officials said.
 
For newer FTAs, the commerce department is seeking to improve access through a digital platform that provides exporters and entrepreneurs with information on market regulations, sectoral opportunities, export trends and benefits available under trade agreements.
 
Anil Bharadwaj, secretary general of the Federation of Indian Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (FISME), said small exporters needed access to consultants and experts who could identify gaps in their processes, product standards and packaging.  “This is especially true in the case of developed economies such as the European Union, Japan, Australia, where exporters need to meet the standards by bearing the process cost -- which is difficult for a micro or a small exporter to bear,” he said.
 
Ajay Sahai, director general and chief executive of the Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO), said limited awareness among small exporters remained a major constraint, although government outreach and digitisation were helping address it.
 
“The government is stepping up outreach to help small exporters understand the tariff preferences available under these agreements and how to claim them. The shift to online issuance of certificates of origin, which exporters use to claim preferential tariff treatment, has also made the process simpler and faster,” Sahai said.
 
As more exporters become aware of the concessions and find it easier to access them, utilisation rates should rise, he added.

data.title: Cabinet clears fresh women's reservation Bill with 50% seat rise formula
data.description:
The Union Cabinet on Friday approved a fresh delimitation-linked women’s reservation Constitution Amendment Bill, which, government sources said, had hard-coded in its text a uniform 50 per cent rise in Lok Sabha seats for all states.  
 
Copies of the Bill are yet to be circulated among lawmakers.
 
The formula, sources said, would assuage the concern of the southern states, and help pave the way for its passage in the special session of Parliament next week.
 
In April, the government had insisted that no state’s share of seats in the Lok Sabha would decline, but didn’t include any such guarantee in the text of the Bill. The Bill fell 54 votes short of the two-thirds mark, which is required for the passage of a Constitution amendment. But the arithmetic has changed since that defeat nearly eight months ago.
 
 
The split in the Trinamool Congress led to 20 of its Lok Sabha members joining the fledgling Nationalist Citizens Party of India, which is now a constituent of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA). Six of the Shiv Sena (UBT)’s parliamentarians joined the Shiv Sena, and the return of the Shiromani Akali Dal, which has one Lok Sabha member, to the NDA has increased the ruling alliance’s numbers.
 
There were indications on Friday evening that the government proposal of 50 per cent increase in seats of all states based on the 1971 Census, and delimitation based on the 2011 Census, could persuade the Congress’ current and former allies, particularly the Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar), which has eight Lok Sabha members, and the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), which has 22. The two parties had helped defeat a similar Bill during the hastily convened special session in April. There were also fears in the Opposition camp of several of its members of Parliament being absent on the day of the voting on the Bill.
 
The Congress convened a meeting of its INDIA (Indian National Inclusive Development Alliance) on Saturday morning, and invited the DMK, its former ally. Its Parliamentary Strategy Group held a meeting on Friday evening, and the party later alleged that the ultimate objective of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) was gerrymandering of constituencies, as was done in Assam and Jammu and Kashmir, in the garb of women’s reservation. The party said the BJP had “treated the Election Commission like a puppet”, and a delimitation exercise would follow a similar course.
 
In Chennai, DMK President M K Stalin said that under no circumstances should Tamil Nadu’s existing 7.18 per cent share of seats in the Lok Sabha be reduced. He also hit out at the Congress, which joined the TVK alliance and the government led by it, after the DMK was defeated in the Assembly polls held earlier this year. Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) Working President Supriya Sule said she would not attend the INDIA bloc’s meeting on Saturday because her father, Sharad Pawar, was ailing, but another leader said the party would support the Bill.  
 
The proposed amendment seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from the present 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation. The Treasury Benches said the move would pave the way for the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state legislative assemblies ahead of the 2029 general election. The fresh Bill seeks to use the 2011 Census to redraw the increased seats. The Cabinet meeting was chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and was convened at 1 pm at Sewa Teerth. The government has called for a four-day special sitting — on November 30 and December 1 in the Lok Sabha, and on December 2 and 3 in the Rajya Sabha.
 
At a media conference in New Delhi, Independent Rajya Sabha Member Kapil Sibal appealed to Opposition parties to ensure that the delimitation Bill had the provision that instead of a retired judge, there should be a retired judge nominated by the government and a retired judge nominated by the Opposition, and they together should choose a third judge to form a three-member delimitation panel.
 
Sibal also highlighted the delay in the case seeking the disqualification of the Trinamool Congress and Shiv Sena (UBT) rebels. Sibal said Parliament would be “defanged”, with no debates and transparency.
 
Between April and now, the BJP has used all its might and persuasive power through agencies and other means to persuade some members, who are part of the Opposition, to agree to this formula, he claimed.
 
(With inputs from Agencies)

data.title: Retail investors must be cautious before chasing FPIs' momentum picks
data.description:
Stocks with high foreign ownership rallied sharply over the past month as foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) pumped nearly ₹1.4 trillion into Indian equities since the start of November. However, analysts said retail investors should look at who owns these stocks and who may sell before chasing hot foreign money. 
Over the past month, the Nifty is up 13.8 per cent while the Nifty FPI 150 index is up 11 per cent. But if we look at the top 15 companies with the highest FPI holdings, then the market cap (mcap) of these firms is up by 23 per cent. 
FPIs, or overseas funds that buy listed shares, own an average 53.4 per cent of these 15 companies. Domestic institutional investors (DIIs), such as mutual funds and insurers, own another 20.4 per cent. But some of these companies have foreign holdings through foreign corporate bodies and that gets classified as FPIs. 
For example, one manufacturing stock has 7 per cent FPI holding and foreign companies together hold more than 55 per cent in it. It is classified as FPI favourite. The stock’s one-month return was 30 per cent as of November 26. A fintech stock, where FPI holding is 4.05 per cent and foreign companies hold 60.12 per cent, also returned 30 per cent over the past month. 
“High foreign ownership in this list is not the same thing as fresh FPI buying,” said Gaurav Arora, head of research at SAHI, a discount broker and trading platform for equities, derivatives and commodities. 
He added, “In these, a large part of the foreign stake is pre-initial public offering (pre-IPO) venture and private equity capital that became public shareholding on listing.” Five among the 15 companies that recently listed are Zetwerk, Turtlemint, Meesho, Groww (Billionbrains) and Urban Company. Apurva Sheth, head of research at Samco Securities, called for tracking how foreign holding changes over time. 
 
“A useful trend for retail investors to track is whether FPIs have consistently increased their stake in a company over the past 
2-4 quarters,” he said. 
“This can be corroborated with FPI sectoral purchase and selling data, published every fortnight. It shows whether institutional interest in the sector is strengthening or beginning to taper off.” 
 
The rally in these stocks may already be slowing. Over the past week, the 15 stocks only gained an average 2.5 per cent. “Retail investors should treat this as two lists, not one,” said Arora. 
“The lenders and hospital chains are long-term holdings where entry price matters more than the latest month's return.”
He said that in the newly-listed names, early foreign backers are potential sellers, and while some are already out of lock-in.
“So, a high FPI stake may be supply waiting to come, not just a vote of confidence,” he said.  
Sheth also said investors should watch promoters, founders or groups that control a company. 
“A consistent increase in promoters’ shareholding can be a positive signal, as it reflects greater skin in the game. Promoters also tend to have a deeper understanding of a business and its prospects compared to external investors. This makes changes in their ownership worth tracking.”

data.title: RBI allows banks to place debit holds on highly suspicious transactions
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has allowed banks to hold a debit transaction if the lender assesses it as highly suspicious, while putting in place a uniform, time-bound procedure for actions with respect to such transactions.
 
The directions will come into effect no later than July 1, 2027.
 
The RBI has directed banks, by way of a standard operating procedure (SOP), to identify, while protecting genuine customers from inconvenience, highly suspicious transactions and accounts, including those linked to money mule activity, cyber-enabled and other financial frauds, or relating to transactions involving terrorist financing on one’s own behalf or on behalf of another person.
 
 
According to the directions, “Highly Suspicious account” means a money mule account or a bank account used on one’s own behalf, knowingly or unknowingly, to receive, layer or transfer proceeds of an offence as specified by law, or of a financial fraud, or transactions involving terrorist financing, where the bank in its assessment considers the account as highly suspicious requiring further actions such as placing a debit hold.
 
“All accounts involving suspicious transactions are not necessarily highly suspicious accounts,” it was clarified.
 
The RBI has said “Money Mule Account” means an account used on behalf of another person, knowingly or unknowingly, to receive, layer or transfer proceeds of an offence or of a financial fraud, or an account relating to transactions involving terrorist financing.
 
Banks have to maintain all necessary information with respect to the amounts and accounts placed on debit hold, including the dates of placing and releasing the debit hold, reasons for the same, and details of correspondence with the account holder and the jurisdictional police authority, for a period of five years from the date of placing the debit hold.
 
As part of the SOP, a bank has been asked to put in place suitable technological solutions to identify highly suspicious transactions and accounts, based on objective parameters, while mitigating the risk of erroneously identifying genuine transactions.
 
“Upon placing the debit hold, the bank shall promptly notify the account holder, if communicating through digital mode (if mobile number / email address is on record), otherwise by the End of Day (EOD) of the next working day,” the directions said.
 
On reporting to the jurisdictional police authority, the bank shall conduct enhanced due diligence (EDD) of the account, it said.

data.title: Adani Group eyes airline investments months after ruling out airline entry
data.description:
The diversified Adani group, which runs multiple airports across the country, has requested the government to allow it to invest in the airline sector, a top official said on Friday.

Group chief finance officer Jugeshinder Robbie Singh told reporters that over 60 crore people in the country can fly, and the number of daily flights needs to go up by nearly 10 times to 30,000.

"And that's why we requested the government to at least allow us to invest, so that we can facilitate the development of airlines. Some fund, some other airline company and things like that...or an entrepreneur who wants to go into that space," the CFO said while speaking on the sidelines of the India Debt Capital Market Summit here.

 

In July this year, the group said it was "not evaluating any proposal to enter the airlines business". On November 3, Adani Airport Holdings chief executive Arun Bansal had ruled out entering the airlines business, saying that it is never a good strategy to compete with customers.

Adani group runs eight airports in the country, including the ones in the financial capital and the satellite city of Navi Mumbai, and also Ahmedabad, Lucknow and Guwahati, which ferry over one-fourth of the country's air passenger traffic.

The airline business has been reduced to a virtual duopoly with two strong domestic carriers -- the Tata Group-led Air India and Rahul Bhatia-run IndiGo, ruling the skies with a 90 per cent market share.

Problems at IndiGo last year, which led to thousands of flight cancellations, led to voices demanding more airlines to operate in the country.

data.title: Datanomics: Hit-and-run deaths in India increase 64% in a decade
data.description: Over the past week, several hit-and-run incidents have been reported across the country. On November 26, a man was injured after an unidentified scooter rider hit him and fled in Gurugram. On November 23, a pedestrian was killed in a hit-and-run incident in Chennai. On November 22, a boy in Gujarat was struck by an SUV and died a day later. These incidents highlight the persistent problem of hit-and-run cases in India. The number of hit-and-run cases in the country increased from 57,083 in 2015 to 69,621 in 2019, before declining to 52,448 in 2020. The figure subsequently rose to 68,783 in 2023 and edged down to 68,584 in 2024. Meanwhile, deaths in hit-and-run accidents increased from 20,709 in 2015 to 34,030 in 2024, registering a growth of 64.3 per cent. A category-wise breakdown of road accidents shows that rear-end collisions, head-on collisions, and side-impact collisions are the three most common types, followed by hit-and-run accidents. Data on road accident deaths per million population across six countries with highest gross domestic product (GDP) shows that most recorded a decline in 2024, while India bucked the trend. Data for China was not available for 2024.

data.title: HSBC India consolidates finance support functions, seeks staff relocation
data.description:
HSBC India is consolidating its finance support functions and has asked employees to relocate to Bengaluru, Gurugram, and Chennai. The London-headquartered lender has asked staff from Kolkata, Hyderabad, and Pune to relocate to those centres. Job losses due to this exercise would be minimal, sources said. HSBC’s India support function has around 48,000 staff.
 
In a statement, an HSBC spokesperson said the changes were part of the bank's efforts to simplify operations and ensure that roles were located where they could best support customers.
 
"As we simplify the bank, our focus remains on ensuring we have the right roles in the right locations to support the best customer outcomes," the spokesperson said.
 
 
The bank is centralising finance support functions in Chennai, Gurugram, and Bengaluru, while phasing out similar roles in other locations. The restructuring is limited to finance functions within the bank's global capability centres (GCCs) in India.
 
HSBC's India GCCs support its global businesses through activities spanning enterprise platforms, analytics and artificial intelligence (AI), risk and controls, and finance and trade operations. Its technology centres also work on automation, data engineering, machine learning, biometrics, and cloud computing, according to the bank's website.
 
According to its annual report, HSBC had 208,720 full-time equivalent employees globally as of December 31, 2025, of whom 47,423 were part of HSBC India. The number of employees in India rose to 48,114 by the end of June 2026.
 
According to a report by Bloomberg, HSBC has been weighing deep job cuts over the coming years as Chief Executive Officer Georges Elhedery deploys AI to shrink its middle and back offices. Non-client-facing roles in global service centres are among those expected to be most affected, people familiar with the matter have said previously. The changes could ultimately affect around 20,000 roles — or about 10 per cent of its total workforce.
 
The consolidation is part of HSBC's broader effort to simplify operations, rationalise costs, and accelerate the adoption of AI, particularly across middle- and back-office functions. The bank has been weighing global workforce reductions of around 20,000 positions over the coming years, or approximately 10 per cent of its workforce, as part of the restructuring, the report said.
 
India has been a key market for HSBC, which emerged as the leading international bank facilitating fundraising by Indian companies through G3 bonds, syndicated loans, and initial public offerings (IPOs) in January-September 2026, leveraging its extensive corporate and institutional relationships and its ability to connect borrowers with pools of capital seeking investment opportunities across debt and equity markets.

data.title: Zee Entertainment buyback to open on Dec 1, set to close on Dec 7
data.description:
Zee Entertainment Enterprises will open its share buyback offer on December 1 and close it on December 7, according to a stock exchange filing by the company on Friday.
 
The company submitted its letter of offer and the tender forms for the proposed buyback to the stock exchanges.
 
Under the buyback, Zee Entertainment plans to buy back up to 65.93 million fully paid-up equity shares with a face value of ₹1 each. The total buyback size is capped at ₹600 crore. The buyback price is ₹91 per share, and the company's share price closed 1.5 per cent higher at ₹67.05 on Friday.
 
 
On November 12, the board of the company approved the buyback.
 
The buyback will be conducted through the tender offer route, allowing eligible shareholders to tender their shares in accordance with the terms set out in the letter of offer.
 
Shareholders wishing to participate in the buyback must submit their completed tender forms and other specified documents to the registrar by December 7, the last date of the offer.
 
The settlement of bids on the stock exchanges is scheduled to be completed by December 14.

data.title: PLI scheme to help telecom firms stay competitive amid US tariffs: Scindia
data.description:
Indian manufacturers, particularly telecom equipment makers, were globally competitive and would remain so on the back of the production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme, even amid proposed US tariffs, said Telecom Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia.
 
"Our PLI scheme has done extremely well, over 100,000 crores in sales, over close to 36,000 crores in exports and I think India has always been competitive and will continue to remain competitive," the minister said, speaking on the sidelines of a briefing on the Department of Posts on Thursday.
 
His remarks came a day after the US proposed a fresh round of tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods, although the proposed rate could be lowered to 17 per cent if India and the US reach a trade agreement.
  
Under the PLI scheme for telecom and network equipment, India has exported just about $1 billion worth of telecom products, accounting for 0.23 per cent of India's overall exports as of 2024, according to data from Niti Aayog. Imports remained high at $3.6 billion.
 
Telecom equipment makers said they were in a wait-and-watch mode as the final tariffs were yet to be decided, and some products, such as smartphones and routers, remained outside the purview of the tariffs.
 
According to some executives, exports of optical fibre, optical fibre cables, base stations, antennas, customer premises equipment, and components to the US were limited and would remain at existing levels until January.
 
"While its too early to say anything with certainty, the existing tariffs will continue to hold till the new ones get notified," said an executive from the industry body representing telecom equipment manufacturers in India.
 
"We're evaluating this, although these tariffs are currently as a proposal level," said another executive from a leading telecom equipment maker who did not want to be identified.
 
Rohan Lobo, partner and industry leader – technology, media and telecommunications, Deloitte South Asia, said that the impact was likely to be uneven since smartphones accounted for a large component of India's telecom-related exports and were outside the purview of both the additional US duty currently in force and the higher tariff proposed on November 25, 2026.
 
"Exposure is likely to be in a small but growing segment primarily in optical fiber and cable, base stations, antennas, and components. There are three factors that are likely to shape the outcome. Firstly, the final scope of product exemptions is still open to consultation. Secondly, the progress of the India–US trade agreement and the possibility of negotiated rate. Thirdly, India's position relative to other competing manufacturing locations like Thailand and Malaysia where the rate proposed is 18 per cent," Lobo said.
 
India has disputed the United States Trade Representative's (USTR's) findings on structural excess capacity and reiterated its commitment to ongoing bilateral trade negotiations.
 
Lobo noted that routers were exempt from the proposed tariff, but there had been barriers to importing foreign-made consumer routers since March 2026. "Similarly, AI data-center demand has left US fiber in short supply and buyers may not have a choice but to absorb the duty," he added.
